title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as on pp. 89-91. E and E' are sets, each carrying a family of distinguished 'saturated' or 'closed' subsets, Σ_E and Σ_{E'}. Each family is a complete lattice, with Sup^Σ the closure of the union, written Sup°_E or sat_W. A relation |∘| expresses 'orthogonality' or incidence between subsets (and points) of E, resp. E'. A correspondence α : E → P(E') induces two things.

- α' : E → Σ_{E'}, with α'(x) = Sup°_{E'}(α(x)).
- α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'}, with α_*(S) = Sup^{Σ_{E'}}_{x∈S} α'(x).

The previous page proved α_*(Sup°_E(x)) = α'(x). So α' and α_* determine each other. The NB box records this: α ↦ (α' ↔ α_*), and likewise β ↦ (β' ↔ β_*).

The page then makes a uniqueness claim. For α given, the transpose β_* (equivalently β') is uniquely determined by the conditions of the proposition. The reason: an element β_*(S') of Σ_E is known once one knows which S ∈ Σ_E satisfy S |∘| β_*(S'). By the transposition condition, these are exactly the S with α_*(S) |∘| S'. This is the adjunction/polarity identity S ⊥ β_*(S') ⇔ α_*(S) ⊥ S'. Uniqueness then follows because saturated sets are determined by their orthogonals; this is implicitly the defining property of Σ, closed = biorthogonal.

A marginal note adds that α' is determined by α, β' by β, and β' is the transpose of α'.

The remaining task is stated next. Characterise those α : E → Σ_{E'} (equivalently α_* sup-generated by α) for which a transpose β : E' → Σ_E exists, with β_*(S') = Sup^{Σ_E}_{x'∈S'} β(x'). Equivalently, one may work with α : E → P(E') instead of E → Σ_{E'}.

The next page answers this with a Proposition. A transpose exists iff α_* preserves arbitrary sups, iff preimages {x | α(x) ⊂ S'} of saturated sets are saturated, iff {x | α(x) |∘| x'} ∈ Σ_E. In modern terms these are morphisms of closure spaces / polarities: the Galois-connection or Chu-space morphism condition, adjoint pairs between complete lattices of closed sets.
errors: In the line 'β : E' → Σ_{E'}' the manuscript itself writes Σ_{E'}; it should be Σ_E (a slip, corrected implicitly by the β_* formula below it).

The uniqueness argument tacitly uses that an element of Σ_E is determined by the set of elements of Σ_E orthogonal to it (closed = biorthogonal). This is not restated here but presumably holds by the definition of Σ via |∘|.

ideas.what: Correspondence α : E → P(E') induces α' : E → Σ_{E'} and a sup-generated map α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'}, which determine each other
ideas.modern_name: Free sup-lattice extension / Kleisli-type extension for the closure monad
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Birkhoff, Ore on Galois connections and closure operators; Joyal–Tierney on sup-lattices)

ideas.what: Transpose β_* uniquely determined by S ⊥ β_*(S') ⇔ α_*(S) ⊥ S'
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint/transpose with respect to a polarity; Chu-space morphism; bonds in formal concept analysis

ideas.what: Existence of transpose iff α_* preserves arbitrary sups (stated on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint functor theorem for complete lattices / continuity of maps between closure spaces

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step in a lattice-theoretic duality: uniqueness of the transpose of a correspondence between closure/orthogonality spaces. This is standard Galois-connection / Chu-space material, and nothing here goes beyond known results.
transcription_corrections: 'je dis que si pour α (= α', α_*) donné' should read 'je dis que pour α (ou α', α_*) donné, β_* (ou β') est déterminé de façon unique par les conditions de la proposition'.
'quand on connaît les S ∈ Σ_E tels que' is fine; the image reads 'dès que' / 'tels que' ambiguously.
In the image the β line reads 'β : E' → Σ_{E'}' (author's slip), not Σ_E.
Final lines read approximately: 'transposée. Ou, ce qui revient au même = partie des α : E → P(E') au lieu de (ald) E → Σ_{E'}'. 'ald' is likely an abbreviation of 'au lieu de'.
The page carries the author's number 90 at top; 93 is the archive foliation.
